cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to the believers in Rome (Romans 1:1, 7). He's just told them they're God's children and co-heirs with Christ, if they suffer with Him so they'll be glorified with Him (Romans 8:16-17). Now he sets the suffering and the glory side by side.

cards.question: Paul weighs our present sufferings against the glory that will be revealed in us. What does he conclude?

answers.text: The sufferings are not comparable to the glory
The sufferings are about equal to the glory
The sufferings will last longer than the glory

cards.text: Then Paul zooms out past people. The creation itself is waiting, and not bored waiting, EAGER waiting, like me pressed up against the oven window for the last two minutes of a batch.

cards.question: Paul says the creation waits in eager expectation for the revelation of the ___ of God.

cards.text: Paul says the creation was subjected to futility. Friend, I KNOW futility. Years in the back of a junk drawer, and not ONE cookie came out of it.

cards.question: Paul says the creation was subjected to futility by its own will.
Paul says the creation was subjected to futility in hope. What is that hope for the creation?

answers.text: To be set free from its decay
To be judged for its decay

cards.question: Paul says the creation will be brought into the glorious ___ of the ___ of God.

cards.text: Then Paul says the whole creation has been groaning together until now. And he's not talking about the groan you make when your alarm goes off. He's got a very specific kind of pain in mind.

cards.question: Paul says the whole creation has been groaning together until the present time. What pains does he compare it to?

answers.text: The pains of a long illness
The pains of a hard famine

cards.text: Not only that. Paul says we who have the firstfruits of the Spirit groan inwardly too, like I do when a whole tray sticks to the pan and I smile like it's FINE.

cards.question: While believers groan inwardly, Paul says they wait eagerly for something. What is it?

answers.text: A rest from all their labor
A home in the promised land

cards.text: Paul says in this hope we were saved. Then he asks a question that answers itself: "Who hopes for what he can already see?"

cards.question: Paul says hope that is seen is still real hope.
If we hope for what we do not yet see, Paul says we wait for it ___.

cards.text: Patiently. Friend, I used to open the oven door every minute to check a batch, and every one of those batches came out FLAT.
In the same way, Paul says, the Spirit helps us in our weakness. And he names one weakness in particular.

cards.question: Paul says we always know how we ought to pray.

cards.text: Ever start a prayer and get stuck right after "Lord…"? Me too, friend, and Paul says the Spirit Himself intercedes for us.

cards.question: Paul says the Spirit intercedes for us with groans too deep for ___.

cards.text: Then Paul says He who searches our hearts knows the mind of the Spirit. And Paul tells us why.

cards.question: Paul says the Spirit intercedes for the saints according to the will of God.

cards.text: Then comes a line a lot of believers know by heart: we know that God works all things together for good. ALL things, friend, not just the batches that come out pretty.

cards.question: Paul says God works all things together for the good of certain people. Who are they?

cards.text: Then Paul goes back further. He says those God foreknew, He also predestined.

cards.question: Paul says those God foreknew, He predestined for something. What is it?

answers.text: To be conformed to the image of His Son
To be kept safe from every hardship
To be given a land of their own

cards.question: Paul says God's Son would be the only one in God's family, with no brothers at all.

cards.text: Then Paul links it all together like a chain. Those He predestined, He also called, and those He called, He also justified.

cards.question: Paul's chain keeps going past those God justified. Where does it end?

cards.text: Glorified. Paul started this whole stretch with glory (Romans 8:18), and he lands right back on it, and friend, God took me from a junk drawer to a GOLD BASE, and that doesn't come close.

findings.problem: The opening card states facts from Romans 1:1, 1:7 and Romans 8:16-17, and it sets up 8:18. Its "verses" field cites only Romans 8:16-17. The rule says a story card cites from the first verse it uses to the last, which here would run from Romans 1:1 to Romans 8:18. That range makes no sense. The Romans 1 references also appear only inline in the text.
findings.question: How should an opening card cite context from outside the passage that comes from more than one place (Romans 1:1, 7 and Romans 8:16-17)? Should the "verses" field hold only the passage verses it sets up, only the outside verses, or something else, with any other references inline?

findings.problem: The question frames the answer as "that hope for the creation." That rules out both wrong answers on its face, because being judged for decay and carrying decay forever aren't hopes. Only the right answer fits the word "hope."

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Romans 8:23 says believers wait eagerly for "our adoption as sons, the redemption of our bodies." No card mentions adoption as sons. That is a key detail of the verse, and it ties into the sons and children of God in 8:19 and 8:21.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This card only repeats "Patiently" from the answer to card 15 and adds a joke. It cites 8:25, which card 15 already covered, and it doesn't carry the baker to any new moment in the passage.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: Romans 8:28 also describes these people as those "who are called according to His purpose." That phrase is never told. It sets up "called" in the chain in 8:30, which card 12 then presents with no link back.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The right answer, "To be conformed to the image of His Son," uses Bible wording and is longer. The wrong answers are plain modern phrases ("To be kept safe from every hardship," "To be given a land of their own"), so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The purpose clause in 8:29, "so that He would be the firstborn among many brothers," only shows up as a false statement about having "no brothers at all." No card ever tells the baker that the Son is the firstborn among many brothers.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This is a recap card. It looks back over 8:18-30 ("Paul started this whole stretch with glory... and he lands right back on it") and tells no new part of the passage. Card 13 already covered 8:30.

The joke "God took me from a junk drawer to a GOLD BASE, and that doesn't come close" doesn't click. It's unclear what "doesn't come close" to what. The line is one long sentence joined by commas that a baker would have to work out.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: Most of stop 2's story cards (1, 5, 9, 12) are flat narration with no reaction, comparison or disbelief. Papa Dorin reads like a pleasant narrator here, not laugh-out-loud funny. The only real joke in the stop (card 14) doesn't land.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
